description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 ~12:45 UTC PendulumHealth reported severe request latency and token cost spikes from their dedicated GPU pool. Customers observed large numbers of 5xx/429s followed by long tail latencies and partial completions. Impact: customer-facing application degraded, multiple transactions timed out.

Impact:
- PendulumHealth experienced ~40% request error rate and 8x token-cost spike during the window.
- Streaming responses truncated for ~18 minutes for a subset of requests.
- Potential billing exposure due to repeat retries and duplicate completions.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in prod us-east
- Models: redwood-7b / redwood-7b-quant pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (customer traces):
1) Customer sent a burst of long-sequence chat completions from a queued job agent at ~12:40 UTC.
2) Client observed repeated 429s and retried aggressively (no exponential backoff).
3) Serving requests consumed all hot worker slots; autoscaler did not immediately provision additional workers due to min_available_workers threshold mismatch.

Observed behavior and logs:
- Frontline logs show worker-slot exhaustion: "worker_pool: available_slots=0" repeated.
- Autoscaler logs: evaluation interval 30s, last scale event 12:10 UTC; recent scale decisions skipped due to perceived transient load (threshold set too high).
- Router traces show multiple retry loops with identical request IDs from PendulumHealth customer agent.

Customer report excerpt: "We saw the UI grind to a halt and then many failed completions; traffic was within our expected range and no backoff was applied on our side — we will investigate client retries but need a mitigation and credit for costs."
comments: 2026-03-10 13:00 UTC — Support (Sofia Martinez): Acknowledged. Triage started; contacting SRE and paging autoscaler owners. SLA first response met.
2026-03-10 13:10 UTC — SRE (Devon Clark): Observed worker slot exhaustion in pendulum pool; investigating autoscaler decisions and recent config changes. Punting to on-call infra lead if required.

2026-03-10 13:28 UTC — SRE (Anika Rao): Applied temporary mitigation: increased dedicated pool max-capacity by +30% and injected emergency routing headroom. Error rate reduced; streaming resumed for most flows.
2026-03-10 15:05 UTC — Support (Sofia Martinez): Customer confirmed service recovery and reported reduced error rates. Initiated billing review for duplicate completions and retry-cost exposure.
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC — PM (Liam O'Neal): Scheduled follow-up call with PendulumHealth for 2026-03-12. Action items assigned for autoscaler config audit and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sudden client retry storm consumed hot slots and prevented new worker provisioning due to overly conservative autoscaler thresholds (min_available_workers set above intended value after recent commit).
Metric evidence: worker_pool.available_slots dropped to 0 at 12:42 UTC; queue_length spiked to 120; autoscaler decision log shows 'skip_scale=true' because 'scale_margin < margin_threshold'.

Traffic pattern: high-concurrency long-sequence completions from a single client agent creating head-of-line blocking and blocking the continuous batching optimization, increasing per-request GPU time.

Configuration change identified: 2026-03-08 deploy included autoscaler threshold change (PR #1287) that increased margin_threshold to avoid churn during short spikes — regression for dedicated, high-latency workloads.
Repro steps constructed in staging: replayed PendulumHealth traces (sanitized) with aggressive client retries and observed identical slot exhaustion and delayed scale-up behavior.
workarounds: Temporary mitigation applied: emergency pool capacity increase (+30%) and dynamic route throttling for the customer's API key to smooth retry amplification.
Advised customer to implement exponential backoff on client retry logic; provided sample backoff config and recommended max_retries=3.
If immediate degradation observed again, customer can request manual pool expansion via dedicated-support channel.
resolution: Hotfix: reverted the autoscaler margin_threshold change from PR #1287 for dedicated pools (rollback applied 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC).

Permanent fix: updated autoscaler logic to consider long-request worker occupancy and introduced a secondary fast-path scale-up when queue_length > 50 for >30s. Change merged in runtime repo PR #1294 and scheduled for controlled rollout.

Operational changes: added dedicated-pool runbook section for retry storms, instrumented alert 'dedicated-pool-sustained-slot-exhaustion' with playbook steps, and created canary tests to exercise scale-up fast-path.

Customer remediation: applied a billing credit of $12,000 to PendulumHealth account to offset retry-related token costs and duplicate completions during the incident window. Customer accepted credit and escalated ask for an on-call postmortem review.
Communication: post-incident call scheduled and summary shared via the Confluence page. Follow-up actions assigned and tracked under INT-4412 and SUP-100721.
post_incident_action_items: ENG-ALGO: Complete autoscaler fast-path rollout and validate in dedicated pools (owner: Devon Clark) — due 2026-03-20.
DOCS: Update dedicated runbook with retry-storm mitigation steps and include sample rate-limit policy (owner: Anika Rao) — due 2026-03-14.
CUSTOMER: Review PendulumHealth client retry config in joint session and share best-practice SDK patch (owner: Sofia Martinez) — meeting 2026-03-12.
BILLING: Finalize and document applied credit, add note to invoice and close billing dispute (owner: Maya Patel) — due 2026-03-13.
